decision_reason: Open Zaakbrug is a municipality-led, versioned Java bridge that lets legacy ZDS case-management applications communicate with the newer ZGW/OpenZaak APIs. The municipal repository supplies an EUPL-1.2 grant, installation documentation, Docker distribution, and a current versioned release; its README identifies municipal production deployments. This is an operational migration tool, not the OpenZaak case system itself.

government_provenance.note: The verified Gemeente Súdwest-Fryslân organization publishes this exact repo. Its README says the bridge began in 2019 with Súdwest-Fryslân, Utrecht, and Haarlem and VNG innovation funding; it lists the municipality and other municipal production uses.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Java application, configuration, tests, documentation, Docker build/distribution links, and source history without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the root EUPL v1.2 license text; GitHub also detects EUPL-1.2. The first located root grant-bearing commit is 2020-10-01: https://github.com/Sudwest-Fryslan/OpenZaakBrug/commit/4a40f8c152da6247c6833dc75db966d4541199f0.

primary_evidence.note: The exact project README states Súdwest-Fryslân went into production in 2021, Haarlem in 2023, and Den Haag in 2024, lists supported legacy applications, and links installation guidance. Version 1.2.21 was released on 2025-11-21: https://github.com/Sudwest-Fryslan/OpenZaakBrug/releases/tag/1.2.21.

product_identity: Open Zaakbrug (legacy ZDS-to-ZGW migration and replication bridge)
agency: Municipality of Súdwest-Fryslân (initial collaboration with Utrecht and Haarlem; VNG innovation subsidy)
family_note: The Súdwest-Fryslân repository is the maintained municipal fork of Haarlem/zds-stuf-to-zgw-api-translator and the versioned Open Zaakbrug implementation used in production. Treat it and its Haarlem ancestor as one bridge product family, not two independent products; it is distinct from OpenZaak itself.
status_note: First located source snapshot with the EUPL grant is 2020-10-01; repository creation predates that. A versioned 1.2.21 release and installation guide are current, and the repository was active in September 2026.

decision_reason: WuppieFuzz is TNO’s supported coverage-guided REST API fuzzer, with an Apache-2.0 source release, installation/tutorial guidance, current versioned installers, and an exact TNO release article. TNO also cites a 2026 scientific publication specifically about this implementation. Third-party dependencies keep their separate licenses.

government_provenance.note: TNO’s official article identifies its new REST API fuzzer, describes the exact tool, links its GitHub repository, and states TNO made it open source. TNO identifies itself as an organisation governed by public law: https://www.tno.nl/en/about-tno/organisation/.

public_source.note: The public Rust source includes a CLI fuzzer, builds, tests, tutorials, release workflows, installers, and a current publiccode.yml.

eligible_license.note: The v1.0.0 release tree contains an Apache-2.0 LICENSE and Cargo.toml identifying TNO as package author. Third-party crates are not relicensed by this grant; their terms are enumerated separately in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.

primary_evidence.note: The official TNO article explains the fuzzer’s end-user function, says it is freely available under Apache-2.0, and links a tutorial. The repository offers installable releases and cites a 2026 paper about WuppieFuzz itself.

agency: Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO)
license: Apache-2.0 (TNO-authored project code; bundled dependencies retain their own licenses)
family_note: WuppieFuzz core is distinct from TNO-S3’s separate language-specific coverage-agent and dashboard repositories; this review does not extend the license or decision to those repos.
status_note: First directly verified licensed functional distribution is release v1.0.0 (2024-09-12), whose tree contains both the source and Apache grant. The current publiccode.yml calls the project stable and identifies TNO; latest observed release v1.7.1 was 2026-08-26. The 2026 citation is product-specific: Rooijakkers et al., “WuppieFuzz: Coverage-Guided, Stateful REST API Fuzzing.”

Although its Hugo/JavaScript site source is public and Apache-2.0 licensed, the product is the curated information resource rather than a government-developed software tool or service in this inventory’s scope.

government_provenance.note: The repository is published under TNO’s verified GitHub organization. TNO states it is an organisation governed by public law; this establishes publisher status, not a software-use claim.

public_source.note: The public repository contains a Hugo site, JavaScript/CSS, deployment configuration, and curated content records.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the root Apache-2.0 license. It covers the repository’s site source; referenced tools, articles, and linked third-party resources remain under their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The README defines the product as a curated list/catalog of SBOM tools, frameworks, blogs, and other media, rendered as a static comparison site. It does not document a separately reusable government software tool or an operational service beyond this informational directory.

product_identity: TNO Awesome SBOM information directory and static comparison site (not a software product for this inventory)
agency: Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO)
license: Apache-2.0 for the site source; linked resource content and third-party software retain their own terms
family_note: A curated SBOM ecosystem information directory, not one of the software tools listed inside it.
status_note: Reject for product scope, not because source or license are unavailable. A separate review could inventory it as a TNO information resource if that is within the catalog mandate.

decision_reason: This is a public codebase for the live Dutch government developer portal, but the assigned Digilab repository’s publiccode.yml points to the older Common Ground/DON repository as canonical source, while its current publiccode names Geonovum as source owner and its README retains a VNG Realisatie 2019 copyright/license notice. It also appears to overlap the separately reviewed API Register, OSS Register, register-site, and knowledge-site repositories. Hold until the current production source boundary, ownership history, and umbrella-versus-component catalog identity are resolved.

government_provenance.note: Geonovum’s 2024 execution plan explicitly says the developer.overheid.nl provision is developed under the Ministry of BZK’s Data bij de Bron program. The exact assigned repo README says it contains the software backing that portal; current publiccode.yml names Stichting Geonovum as code/repository owner, while historical README/license material credits VNG Realisatie.

public_source.note: The assigned GitLab project is publicly readable and contains web, API, data, deployment, and container source. Its README identifies it as software backing developer.overheid.nl.

eligible_license.note: The current source has an EUPL-1.2 root license and publiccode.yml claim. Its publiccode points to the older Common Ground/DON source, whose actual LICENCE.md grants EUPL-1.2 with VNG Realisatie copyright: https://gitlab.com/commonground/don/developer.overheid.nl/-/commit/f7e954952bc9b78495a0b7e70ffc44ed3b3a1ef9. Resolve code-owner history and whether the current copy’s complete additions are in grant scope before admission.

primary_evidence.note: The live official site describes the Dutch government developer portal, and the assigned README says this repo backs it. The full monorepo appears to overlap separately reviewed portal repositories (`don-api-register`, `don-oss-register`, `don-register-site`, and `don-site`); no authoritative current deployment map established whether this repo is the production umbrella, a legacy implementation, or a parallel codebase.

product_identity: Developer Overheid portal software (full-stack API and OSS discovery portal; umbrella/legacy boundary unresolved)
agency: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations (BZK) program; Geonovum is named by current publiccode as source/repository owner; VNG Realisatie is credited by the historical EUPL notice
license: EUPL-1.2 (portal source; repository ownership/attribution and current additions need reconciliation)
family_note: Potential umbrella for the separately reviewed Developer Overheid API Register, OSS Register, shared register-site frontend, and knowledge portal. Avoid a duplicate umbrella/component product entry until the current production deployment boundary is confirmed.
status_note: Current Digilab project was created in 2024; its publiccode.yml points to the Common Ground/DON canonical source. The older upstream has a directly inspected EUPL-1.2 grant-bearing commit in 2019. Do not treat that as proof that every later Digilab contribution or every separately linked component is covered.

decision_reason: This is a public, working reference implementation with source, a live demo, and EUPL terms. Hold because its README still describes LDV as a draft and its conformance claim has not been mapped to Logius's finalized 1.0.0 standard; no versioned release or official production/adoption record for this exact implementation resolves that gap. Clear with current conformance documentation or an official deployment/adoption record tied to this code.

government_provenance.note: The exact government-hosted project metadata identifies Geonovum as main copyright owner and scopes the software to the Dutch government; the repository is published in the Digilab.overheid.nl Logboek Dataverwerkingen group. Logius identifies the Ministry of BZK as responsible for the standard and Logius as its manager: https://www.logius.nl/onze-dienstverlening/gegevensuitwisseling/logboek-dataverwerkingen/over-logboek-dataverwerkingen.

public_source.note: The public repository includes a multi-service implementation, developer setup instructions, tests, and a live demo link; the initial source tree already contains functional backend and frontend code.

eligible_license.note: The exact repository contains the full EUPL-1.2 text and publiccode.yml declares EUPL-1.2 with Geonovum as the main copyright owner. This decision covers the repository-authored program, not separately licensed dependencies.

primary_evidence.note: This live, project-specific demo describes the reference implementation and demonstrates user-facing LDV logging. However, the repo README calls the standard a draft while Logius now publishes finalized LDV 1.0.0 (https://gitdocumentatie.logius.nl/publicatie/logboek/dataverwerkingen/1.0.0/); no exact-version conformance mapping, versioned release, or official operational-use record establishes that this demo implements the finalized standard.

product_identity: LDV Reference Implementation (distributed data-processing log and transparency demo)
agency: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations (standard sponsor); Geonovum (repository copyright owner); Logius (standard manager)
license: EUPL-1.2 for repository-authored code; dependencies retain their own terms
family_note: This is a reference implementation/demo of the Logius LDV standard, not the normative standard itself. Do not merge its software license with the separately published standard documentation.
status_note: The first inspected public commit (2025-05-16) contains functional source and the EUPL-1.2 license text. The project is explicitly marked development and has no GitLab releases/tags. Reassess when the project documents conformance to LDV 1.0.0 or an official agency records use of this exact build.

decision_reason: LX-core is public and the current README explicitly grants EUPL-1.2-or-later to the program except files with different notices. Hold because this repository calls itself a 2025 revised LinkeXtractor version published for review, has no versioned release, and the official service page documents LinkeXtractor generally without showing that the deployed product uses this new core. Keep this as one LinkeXtractor product family until an official deployment/replacement map establishes whether LX-core is a distinct product or merely its new component.

government_provenance.note: KOOP's official page names and describes the exact LinkeXtractor product; its README states LX-core is the new version replacing the older implementation. KOOP became part of Logius in 2023: https://www.logius.nl/actueel/logius-en-koop-samen-een-organisatie. This establishes the product-family sponsor but not deployment of this new repository.

public_source.note: The assigned public repository contains the BaseX/XQuery application and setup/API documentation; its README includes Docker build and run instructions and identifies the required LiDO service dependency.

eligible_license.note: The repository README states: except files with another notice, the program is licensed under EUPL-1.2 or later, and identifies the copyright as the State of the Netherlands and contributors. No separate root LICENSE file is present; the README's project-wide grant is the direct grant inspected. Dependencies retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The official page confirms an operational LinkeXtractor product, but does not identify LX-core as the deployed version. The assigned README says this is a new version published for review, and the repository has no versioned release; exact-product operational use or official release evidence is needed.

product_identity: LinkeXtractor Core (2025 revised core implementation; successor implementation status unresolved)
license: EUPL-1.2-or-later for program files without a different notice; dependencies retain their own terms
family_note: The official LinkeXtractor page documents the mature legacy product, while this repository calls itself a new 2025 version. Treat both as one product family and avoid a separate LX-core catalog identity unless independent use/distribution is established.
status_note: The first inspected commit with the EUPL project-wide README grant and functional source is 2025-04-18. The README says 'published for review'; no release/tag or official deployment mapping was found. Hold until the successor relationship and actual use of this repo are documented.

decision_reason: NLdoc.API is a separately deployable Logius conversion/validation HTTP service with an EUPL-1.2 grant, source, Docker/Helm installation and production instructions, documentation, and a versioned 6.3.2 release. DigiToegankelijk's official announcement says NLdoc was made ready for use and released open source for organizations to deploy themselves. This decision is limited to the API repository, not the entire NLdoc ecosystem.

government_provenance.note: The official DigiToegankelijk/Logius announcement names NLdoc, states Logius made the product available as open source, and links the downloadable GitLab project. The exact assigned repository is under Logius and its README identifies NLdoc.API as developed by Logius.

public_source.note: The public Elixir repository contains the API implementation, tests, container and Helm deployment material, and documentation; it is accessible without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the repository's full EUPL-1.2 LICENSE. The 2025 initial commit already contained the grant and functional API source. This grant is for this API repository; separately packaged NLdoc dependencies and other ecosystem repositories retain their own licenses.

primary_evidence.note: The exact official announcement (11 December 2025) says NLdoc is ready for use, allows organizations to deploy it themselves, and describes its APIs and editor. The API README documents conversion and validation endpoints, Docker/Helm installation, production startup, and its 6.3.2 release; the repository's 6.3.2 release is dated 2025-12-26.

product_identity: NLdoc.API (independently deployable document-conversion and validation API service)
agency: Logius, Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations
license: EUPL-1.2 (this API repo; other NLdoc repositories and dependencies are outside this decision)
family_note: This is the independently deployable API service within the broader NLdoc system. This review does not transfer its EUPL grant to the NLdoc editor, workers, validation engines, or other repositories.
status_note: The first inspected public source-and-license commit is 2025-01-27; the current 6.3.2 versioned release is dated 2025-12-26. The official announcement notes project-team support ended from January 2026; record that support sunset, although the release is less than a year old at this review.

agency: Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO)
license: Not established for this profile-only repository; its README's umbrella Apache-2.0 statement does not grant rights to linked repositories
family_note: The README links separate Rule Editor and Choppr codebases. Review those exact repositories as separate leads; do not infer their source, license, or eligibility from this profile repo.
